video.title: How to Repair Mobile Phones: Step-by-Step Guide

steps: Lay out precision screwdrivers, plastic pry tools, tweezers, suction cup and a mat.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to do before opening a phone?
quiz.explain: Powering off stops short circuits while you work inside.

quiz.q: Why drain a battery below 25 percent before repair?
options: A charged battery is more dangerous if punctured
quiz.explain: A low battery holds less energy, so an accident is less dangerous.

quiz.q: What is a spudger?
options: A plastic tool for prying and unplugging cables
quiz.explain: A spudger is a plastic stick for lifting cables without damage.

days.title: Open a Phone Safely
days.goal: Open a phone without cracking the screen or tearing a cable.
steps: Power the phone off and remove the SIM tray.
Warm the edges gently to soften the glue.
Lift the screen with a suction cup and slide a plastic pick around the edge.
Open the phone like a book, slowly, so no cable tears.
days.task: Open a practice phone and close it again with no damage.
days.challenge: Open a phone without tearing any ribbon cable.

quiz.q: What should you unplug first inside a phone?
quiz.explain: Unplugging the battery first cuts all power to the board.

quiz.q: Why move small parts to the new screen?
options: The earpiece and sensors are needed for the phone to work fully
quiz.explain: Small parts like the earpiece and sensors must move over or features stop working.

quiz.q: Why heat the edges before lifting a screen?
options: To soften the glue holding the screen
quiz.explain: Gentle heat softens the adhesive so the screen lifts without cracking.

days.title: Screen Replacement Basics

Unplug the battery first, then the screen cables.
Move small parts (earpiece, sensors) to the new screen.
Test the new screen before you glue it down.

days.title: Water Damage: First Steps
days.goal: Know what to do first when a phone gets wet.
steps: Power the phone off at once and do not charge it.
Dry the outside and remove the SIM tray.
Never use a hair dryer on high heat.
Open the phone, dry the inside and clean any corrosion (green or white crust).

quiz.q: What should you do with screws when you take a phone apart?
options: Keep them in order so each goes back in the same hole
quiz.explain: Screws are different sizes; keeping them in order means each goes back where it belongs.

quiz.q: When should you test a phone during reassembly?
options: Before you seal the phone, test screen, battery and buttons
quiz.explain: Testing before sealing lets you fix problems while the phone is still open.

quiz.q: What does it mean if screws are left over after reassembly?
options: You missed a screw somewhere and must open the phone again
quiz.explain: Leftover screws mean a part is not fixed properly; open the phone and find where they belong.

capstone.title: Repair a Real Phone
capstone.brief: Repair a real phone for a real person — screen, battery or charging fault — test every function and hand it back working with a warranty note.
checks: Right part ordered for the exact phone model
Repair done with no damage to cables or parts
Screen, battery, charging, sound and cameras all tested
Phone sealed neatly with no leftover screws
Owner shown the fix and how to care for the phone
Price list and warranty note handed over
deliverables: Receipt with parts, time and price
